Sh. Kameshwar Mishra, Ld. Counsel for petitioners.
Driver in person(defence lying struck off vide order dated 23.02.2023).
None for owner(defence lying struck off vide order dated 23.02.2023).
Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

Smt. Laxmi, aged about 70 years (deceased) had suffered fatal injuries in a Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 08.08.2020 at about 6:30 am at Red Light Signal of Majlis Park Metro Station, Road No. 51, Delhi, involving Indica Car bearing registration no. DL12B1425 (offending vehicle) allegedly being driven in a rash and negligent manner by respondent no. 1.
2.

According to Detailed Accident Report (DAR), on 08.08.2020 at about 6:30 am, when Smt.
Laxmi was crossing the road from Majlis Park Red Light signal through Zebra Crossing, offending vehicle which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit her with a great force, as a result of which she fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
She was immediately taken to Loknayak Hospital, New Delhi where she was medically examined and thereafter, she was referred to Sushruta Trauma Centre, Civil Lines, Delhi but was declared dead.
Postmortem was conducted on the body of deceased at the mortuary of BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi.
FIR No. MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 581/20 U/s 279/304A IPC was registered at PS. Adarsh Nagar with regard to said accident.
It is claimed that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and the same was uninsured during the period in question.

3 3.
The respondents no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner failed to file their WS despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities.
Consequently, their defence was struck off vide order dated 23.02.2022 passed by my Ld. Predecessor.

4. In support of their claim, the petitioners have examined eight witnesses i.e. PW1 Sh. Nand Lal (Son of deceased), PW2 Sh. Dilip, PW3 Sh. Saifuddin(eyewitness) , PW4 HC Kaushal Kumar Meena,
PW5 SI Hans Raj, PW6 ASI Avnish Singh, PW7 ASI Om Prakash and PW8 SI Nag Singh(IO of the case) and their evidence was closed vide order dated 29.11.2022.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and their respective evidence was closed vide order dated 24.01.2023.
5. I have already heard the arguments addressed by Ld. Counsels for the parties.
I have also gone through the record.

My findings on the issues are as under: MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS.
Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 6.
For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW3 Sh. Saifuddin is relevant.

In his evidence, he deposed that on 08.08.2020 at about 6:40 AM, he was doing morning walk and when he reached at Majlis Park Red Light, he saw that there was red light signal and an old woman was crossing the road via zebra crossing.

He further deposed that in the meantime, the traffic signal turned green and suddenly the offending vehicle came from Azadpur side and hit his car against an old woman, as a resulf of which she fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
He further deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle made the old woman sit in his car and police came at the spot.
He further deposed that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle.
He had not been crossexamined by any of the respondents despite grant of opportunity.
7. The careful perusal of testimony of aforesaid witness i.e. PW3 would go to show that the respondents have not been able to impeach his testimony through litmus test of crossexamination.

Even otherwise, the testimony of aforesaid witness inspires confidence with regard to his presence at the spot at the time of accident as his name is also mentioned at S.No. 1 in the list of witnesses filed alongwith the chargesheet by the IO in the criminal case.
Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 581/20 u/s 279/304A IPC was registered at PS. Adarsh Nagar with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS.
Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 show that same was registered on 08.08.2020 on the basis of DD Entry No. 0054A(Ex. PW5/1) with regard to accident call received in PS. Adarsh Nagar on 08.08.2020(date of accident itself).
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.

8. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle, was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

4 9.

Not only this, the respondent no. 1 namely Sh. Shyam Saxena (accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC & 3/181, 146/196 M.V. Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Same would also point out towards rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 10.
Copy of MLC (which is part of criminal case record) of deceased would show that she had been removed to Loknayak Hospital, Delhi with alleged history of RTA on 08.08.2020 at 11:20 AM.
Not only this, postmortem was got conducted on the body of deceased.
Copy of PM Report (which is part of DAR) would show that cause of death of deceased was opined due to head injury produced by blunt force/surface impact.
All the injuries were antemortem in nature, fresh in duration prior to death and caused by blunt force/surface impact sufficient to cause death in ordinary course of nature.
The injuries as mentioned in the relevant column of external injuries of the said report, are also consistent with the injuries which are sustained in road traffic accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the aforesaid documents from the side of respondents including insurance company.

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of pre ponderence of probabilities that deceased had sustained fatal injuries in the Motor Vehicular Accident which had taken place on 08.08.2020 at about 6:30 am at Red Light Signal of Majlis Park Metro Station, Road No. 51, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 12.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY/LOSS OF ESTATE 13.
Now, the first question which arises for consideration is as to whether the petitioners are entitled to loss of dependency or loss of estate.
This question came up for consideration on several occasions before our own High Court as well as before various other High Courts.

In the matter titled as "A Manavalagan Vs. A. Krishnamurthy & Ors.", I (2005) ACC 304(DB), Hon'ble Division Bench of Karnataka High Court has summarized the principles enunciated on this issue in para 19 of the judgment.

entities.text: A Manavalagan Vs. A. Krishnamurthy & Ors.", I (2005) ACC 304(DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Division Bench of Karnataka High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Same reads as under: "xxxxxx (i) The law contemplates two categories of damages on the death of a person.
The first is the pecuniary loss sustained by the dependant members of his family as result of such death.
The Nand Lal & Ors. vs . Shyam Saxena & Ors.

entities.text: Nand Lal & Ors. vs . Shyam Saxena & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Page 1 Of 17 on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184470625/
5 second is the loss caused to the estate of the deceased as a result of such death.

In the first category,
the action is brought by the legal representatives, as trustees for the dependants beneficially entitled.

In the second category, the MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
17.03.2023 action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation, when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.

In the first category of cases, the Tribunal in exercise of power under section 168 of the Act, can specify the persons to whom compensation should be paid and also specify how it should be distributed(Note: for example, if the dependants of a deceased Hindu are a widow aged 35 years and mother aged 75 years, irrespective of the fact that they succeed equally under the Hindu Succession Act, the Tribunal may award a larger share to the widow and a smaller share to the mother, as the widow is likely to live longer).
But, in the second category of cases, no such adjustments or alternation of shares is permissible and he entire amount has to be awarded to the benefit of the estate.

Even if the Tribunal wants to specify the sharing of the compensation amount, it may have to divide the amount strictly in accordance with the personal law governing succession, as the amount awarded and recovered forms part of the estate of deceased.
(ii) Where the claim is by the depdendants, the basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants.
A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life, under the head of loss to estate.

(iii) Where the claim by the legal representatives of the deceased who were not dependants of the deceased, then the basis for award of MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
17.03.2023 compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of savings by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life is added.
(iv) The procedure for determination of loss to estate is broadly the same as the procedure for determination of the loss of dependency.
Both involve ascertaining the multiplicand and capitalising it by multiplying it by an appropriate multiplier.
But, the significant difference is in the figure arrived at as multiplicand in cases where the claimants who are dependants claim loss to estate.

The annual contribution to the family constitutes the multiplicand in the case of loss of dependency,
whereas the annual savings of the deceased becomes the multiplicand in the case of loss to estate.
The method of selection of multiplier is however the same in both cases.
xxxxxxx"

14. The aforesaid legal position has been reiterated by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the celebrated decision of "Keith Rowe Vs. Prashant Sagar & Ors.", II(2010) ACC 64 as well as by Hon'ble Karnataka High Court in the case titled as "Jacob Vs. Managing Director, Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation", 2018 ACJ 91.
15.

Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 not loss of dependency, in view of the reason that the Nand Lal & Ors. vs . Shyam Saxena & Ors.

6
claimants have failed to lead any cogent or definite evidence to show that they were financially dependent upon the earnings of deceased at the time of accident.

It is an undisputed fact that deceased Smt. Laxmi was an old aged lady and she was beggar at the time of accident but it is nowhere the case of claimants that they were financially dependent upon her income.
The entire testimony of PW1 is completely silent on this aspect.

16. Though the petitioners have pleaded that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.
25,000/ per month but they have not adduced any evidence to prove the employment and income of deceased.
The petitioners have also not filed any documentary proof of educational qualifications of the deceased.
In these circumstances the income of the deceased is taken as minimum wages of an unskilled worker applicable at the time of accident, which were Rs. 14,842/(date of accident being 08.08.2020).
In view of aforesaid, the petitioners are entitled to 1/3rd of the income towards the loss of Estate i.e. Rs. 4947/(rounded off) per month.
17. As per the case of petitioners, deceased Smt. Laxmi was aged about about 70 years at the time of accident.

In order to prove the age of deceased, the petitioners have relied upon the copy of postmortem report of deceased filed alongwith the DAR which shows the age of the deceased to be 70 years on 08.08.2020.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD: 17.03.2023 to controvert the version of petitioners.
Hence, the deceased is considered around 70 years of age at the time of accident.

Thus, the multiplier of 5 would be applicable in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors."
passed in SLP(Civil) No. 25590/14 decided on 31.10.17.
18.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that deceased was aged about 70 years, no amount is awarded towards future prospects.
Thus, the total of loss of Estate would be Rs.2,96,820/(Rs. 4947 X12 X 5).
Hence, a sum of Rs.2,97,000/(rounded off) is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.
LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION 19.

After the celebrated judgment of "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. mentioned supra and recent judgment titled New India Assurance Company Limited versus Somwati & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 3093 of 2020 dated 07.09.2020 the petitioners are not entitled to be compensated under this head.

LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 20.

In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as New India Assurance Company Limited versus Somwati & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 3093 of 2020, dated 07.09.2020 I am of the considered opinion that petitioner no. 1(son of deceased) and petitioner no. 3 Smt. Banti Bai (daughter of deceased) are entitled for payment of Rs. 40,000/ each towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text: Consequently, a sum of Rs. 80,000/ is awarded to the petitioners under this head.
FUNERAL EXPENSES 21.

In view of the facts and circumstances of the present case and in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors." mentioned supra, a sum of Rs. 15,000/ is awarded in favour of petitioners on account of funeral expenses.

The total compensation is assessed as under:
1. Loss of estate Rs. 2,97,000/ MACP No. 86/21; FIR No. 581/20; PS. Adarsh Nagar DOD:
17.03.2023 2. Loss of Consortium Rs. 80,000/
3. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15000/ Total Rs. 3,92,000/
22.
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Offending vehicle was uninsured at the time of accident.

Respondent no. 1 being principal tortfeasor and respondent no. 2 being owner of the offending vehicle and thus, vicariously liable for the acts of principal tortfeasor, are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount to the petitioner.

23. In view of my aforesaid findings, I award a sum of Rs. 3,92,000/ alongwith interest @ 7% per annum w.e.f date of filing the petition i.e. 04.03.2021 till the date of its realization, in favour of petitioner no. 1 and against both the respondents jointly and severally (Reliance placed on judgment "Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Sangeeta Devi & Ors" bearing MAC. APP. 165/2011 decided on 22.02.2016).
